trap-nonspeakable.notes: FINDINGS (report, not fixed), three items. (1) IT IS NOT A NORM, AND THE BLOCK PROVES IT. The block defines ||delta_k||_F^2 = delta_k . G . delta_k = sum_alpha lambda_alpha c_{k alpha}^2, then - because it has just stated that G is indefinite - defines ||delta_k||_F = sqrt(|sum_alpha lambda_alpha c_{k alpha}^2|). So the quantity written as a squared norm can be NEGATIVE, and ||delta||_F squared is then not equal to ||delta||_F^2. Calling an indefinite quadratic form a Frobenius norm is a misnomer that the block's own preceding sentence refutes; either rename it (a signed Frobenius pairing, with the magnitude taken separately) or state the absolute value at the point of definition rather than two lines later. (2) THIS BLOCK CONTRADICTS THE prop:gram-matrix-h3-symbolic .ts authorNote, and this block is the one that is right. That authorNote (2026-08-08) says 'the main theorem is positive-definiteness for u > 1'; this remark says the Gram matrix is not positive definite, the Lean file GramMatrixH3Symbolic.lean:189 docstring says 'det(G(u)) = -(strictly positive) != 0 for u > 1' (i.e. negative determinant), and both witnesses record a negative eigenvalue. Recorded here as corroboration. (3) UNSOURCED AND CONVENTION-SENSITIVE: 'The boundary neutrons have larger Frobenius norms than the interior neutrons' is asserted with no witness or computation cited; and the Markov-trace decomposition tr_M(x) = sum_lambda z^A / s_lambda(q) chi_lambda(x) is linear in powers of the convention-dependent z, with neither the convention nor the exponent's normalisation stated. Also note the symbol s_lambda(q) is used for the Schur ELEMENT while s_lambda is the standard notation for the Schur FUNCTION - a collision the notation register would want disambiguated.
